name: Mutalyzer_normalize_variant
description: Validate and normalize an HGVS variant description using Mutalyzer. Returns the corrected/normalized HGVS notation, predicted protein effect, RNA description, and gene symbol. Essential for clinical variant interpretation - ensures HGVS nomenclature compliance and predicts amino acid changes. Accepts coding DNA (c.), genomic (g.), protein (p.), or RNA (r.) variant descriptions. Example: 'NM_003002.4:c.274G>T' normalizes to a SDHD missense variant with protein prediction p.(Asp92Tyr).

variant.description: HGVS variant description. Examples: 'NM_003002.4:c.274G>T' (SDHD missense), 'NM_000546.6:c.215C>G' (TP53 p.Pro72Arg), 'NM_000059.4:c.7397C>T' (BRCA2). Format: reference:coordinate_system.change

corrected_description.description: The description after syntactic correction. Differs from the input when the input was malformed but recoverable.

normalized_description.description: The canonical HGVS description. DIFFERENT from the input whenever the input was not canonical -- most commonly because an indel was not 3'-shifted -- and two descriptions that normalise to the same string are the same variant.

gene_id.description: The gene the reference belongs to.

rna_description.description: The variant at RNA level, e.g. 'NM_003002.4:r.(274g>u)'. Parentheses mean predicted rather than observed.

description.description: The protein-level HGVS, e.g. 'NM_003002.4(NP_002993.1):p.(Asp92Tyr)'. Parentheses again mean PREDICTED.

predicted_sequence.description: The protein sequence the variant predicts. Comparing the two shows the consequence directly.

infos.description: Notices Mutalyzer raised about the normalisation. NOT errors -- but 'IMRNAGENOMICTIP' says an mRNA reference was used where a genomic one was meant, which changes what the coordinates refer to.

name: Mutalyzer_back_translate
description: Convert a protein-level HGVS variant to possible DNA-level variant descriptions using Mutalyzer. Given a protein change like NP_002993.1:p.Asp92Tyr, returns the corresponding coding DNA change(s) like NM_003002.4:c.(274G>T). Useful for finding the DNA-level representation of a known amino acid change, accounting for codon degeneracy.

variant.description: Protein-level HGVS variant description. Examples: 'NP_002993.1:p.Asp92Tyr' (SDHD), 'NP_000537.3:p.Pro72Arg' (TP53), 'NP_000050.2:p.Tyr32Cys' (BRCA2). Format: NP_accession:p.AminoAcidChange

count.description: How many DNA descriptions could produce it. More than one is the normal case -- the genetic code is degenerate, so a protein change does not determine the DNA change.

dna_descriptions.description: Every DNA description consistent with the protein variant.

name: Mutalyzer_parse_hgvs
description: Parse an HGVS variant description into a structured model using Mutalyzer. Returns the reference sequence ID, coordinate system (c./g./p./r.), variant type (substitution, deletion, insertion, etc.), and exact positions. Useful for programmatically extracting components of HGVS notation without regex parsing.

variant.description: HGVS variant description to parse. Examples: 'NM_003002.4:c.274G>T', 'NC_000017.11:g.7674220C>G', 'NM_000546.6:c.215C>G'. Supports coding (c.), genomic (g.), protein (p.), and RNA (r.) coordinates.

input_description.description: The HGVS description that was parsed, echoed back.

model.description: The parsed description as a structured model. This is a PARSE, not a validation -- a description can parse and still be wrong about the reference sequence.

type.description: What kind of description it is, e.g. 'description_dna'.

coordinate_system.description: Which coordinate system, e.g. 'c' for coding, 'g' for genomic, 'r' for RNA, 'p' for protein. The same number means different positions in each.

reference.description: The reference sequence the description is against.

id.description: Its accession, e.g. 'NM_003002.4'. The VERSION matters: coordinates can shift between versions.

variants.description: The individual changes the description encodes.

source.description: Where the change was read from, e.g. 'reference'.

type.description: 'point' for a single position, 'range' for a span.

source.description: Whether that came from the description or from the reference.
